Land from Esther Balaton Estate for future urban development.
Funding for acquisition comes from property realized reserve.

chips.text: Recommended

description: Consolidates several city reserve funds, reallocating $1.8M for parks.
Allows roadway reserve to fund land purchases for infrastructure.
Albert Community Centre repairs now use general maintenance reserve.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor Pierce questioned wording on excess self-insured funds, seeking council's decision.
Staff apologized for wording regarding excess self-insured funds, offering clarification.
Staff confirmed no funding is being taken away from parks programs.

description: SREDA and Discover Saskatoon agreements will be monitored.
Progress will be reviewed before agreements expire.
Organizations are asked to bolster strategic collaboration.

chips.text: Recommended
Mayor Block praised clarity on roles and increased collaboration.
Taxpayers fund SREDA and Discover Saskatoon with $2 million annually.
SREDA and Discover Saskatoon CEOs supported the recommendations.

speakers.name: Erin Lawson
said: Supports administration's findings and recommended path forward.
SREDA focuses on long-term economic development, job growth, investment.
City benefits from two organizations with specialized expertise.

speakers.name: Stephanie Pocha
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Saskatoon Regional Economic Development
said: Administration found two distinct, complementary organizations.
Work runs in sequence, making each other more effective.
Supports all three recommendations, including strategic collaboration.

description: Committee recommends direct sale of 902-912 3rd Avenue North for 58-64 affordable units.
This replaces a prior affordable housing plan for 2401 Broadway Avenue.
The Broadway Avenue site was unfeasible due to zoning and public opposition.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor Donauer questioned direct sale, asking if it was the best deal for the land.
Vox Developments Ltd. will build 58-64 affordable housing units, locked for 20 years.
Councillor Pierce asked how to prevent this direct sale from setting a precedent.
Administration could not confirm if other developers were interested in the site.
Community consultation showed significant opposition to rezoning 2401 Broadway Avenue.
Administration is under time pressure to meet Housing Accelerator Fund targets by December 31.

description: Seven high-risk audit recommendations remain outstanding (May 2026).
